learning_outcomes.text: Students should know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students should be able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students should be able to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Ability to direct works and installations of telecommunication systems, complying with current regulations, ensuring service quality.
Ability to lead, plan and supervise multidisciplinary teams.
Ability to prepare, strategic plan, direct, coordinate and manage technical and economic projects in all areas of Telecommunication Engineering following quality and environmental criteria.
Ability to apply the principles of economics and human resource and project management, as well as telecommunications legislation, regulation and standardization.
Ability to model, design, implement, manage, operate, administer and maintain networks, services and content.

Ability to plan, make decisions and package networks, services and applications considering service quality, direct and operational costs, the implementation plan, supervision, security procedures, scaling and maintenance, as well as managing and ensuring quality in the development process.
Familiarize the student with IT management processes.
Introduce the student to IT governance.
Introduce the student to techniques for implementing IT management and governance in companies.
Familiarize the student with international IT management standards: ITIL and ISO 20000.
Familiarize the student with international IT governance standards: COBIT and ISO 38500.
Introduce the student to IT management system audit processes.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of IT Management based on ITIL
Introduction to IT Governance: service strategy
Audit of processes according to ISO 20000
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum of 4 out of 10 points must be obtained in both the Final Exam and the Group Work. Attendance with effective participation in 80% of laboratory practice sessions and public defense of the group work are mandatory. The final grade is calculated as 0.6 * Final Exam (EF) + 0.4 * Group Work (TG), with a minimum overall grade of 5 to pass. If minimums are not met in individual parts, the final grade will be the minimum between the formula result and 4.5. For extraordinary calls, only the group work grade from the ordinary call is retained. The theory exam must be passed with at least 5 points out of 10. For differentiated evaluation, an individual work replaces the group work, and both parts must be passed with at least 5 points.
